an1.198:1.1: He was slow of understanding, rejected even by his brother, but then, supported by the Buddha, he achieved mastery ([thag10.4]()). The younger brother of Mahāpanthaka, he is praised at [ud5.10](), and give effective instruction to the nuns at [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc22:1.1]().
an1.199:1.1: The “evolution of heart” (_cetovivaṭṭa_) and the “evolution of perception” (_saññāvivaṭṭa_) are obscure terms found only here. They are said in the late canon to be the same thing ([ps1.1:503.1]()), although this seems unlikely given that here they are distinguished. Cūḷapanthaka’s story tells of how he was slow of understanding, rejected even by his brother, before developing his mind through meditation. Perhaps “evolution of heart” refers to his remarkable transformation.
an1.200:1.1: His verses are at [thag8.3](), where tells of undertaking the resolve to not sit down until awakened.
